rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$PV=\frac{1}{3}mn\bar{c}^{2},\qquad KE=\frac{3}{2}kT\ (\text{molecule})=\frac{3}{2}RT\ (\text{mole})$$
$$v_{rms}=\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}},\quad \bar{c}=\sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}},\quad v_{mp}=\sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}}$$
$$M=\frac{3RT}{v_{rms}^{2}}$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Molecules keep moving at the rms speed. ✅ Speeds obey a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution; the rms value is only an average measure.  ·  ❌ Kinetic theory says molecules never interact. ✅ Interaction is neglected *except during collisions* — this idealisation is exactly what limits the model.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Maxwell–Boltzmann curve: the fraction of molecules at a given speed falls exponentially at high speed; heating shifts the peak to higher speed.  ·  Mean free path at 1 atm, 300 K ≈ 10⁻⁷ m — about a thousand molecular diameters.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** rms speed of O₂ at 300 K. **Solution:** M = 0.032 kg mol⁻¹; v_rms = √(3 × 8.314 × 300/0.032) ≈ 483 m s⁻¹.  ·  **Problem:** Ratio of rms speeds of H₂ and O₂ at the same temperature. **Solution:** v ∝ 1/√M → v(H₂)/v(O₂) = √(32/2) = 4; hydrogen molecules are four times faster, hence its escape from the atmosphere.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: gaseous state, kinetic theory of gas, its postulates (within States of Matter).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning and purpose  ·  The kinetic theory of gases (Clausius, Maxwell, Boltzmann) explains the measurable behaviour of a gas — pressure, volume, temperature and diffusion — in terms of the motion of its molecules. It converts the empirical gas laws into a mechanical model: pressure arises from molecular collisions with the walls, and temperature measures the average molecular kinetic energy.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: v_mp : c̄ : v_rms = √2 : √(8/π) : √3 ≈ 1 : 1.128 : 1.225.  ·  Ideal gas equation PV = nRT; from kinetic theory P = ⅓ (Nm/m)⟨c²⟩, so PV = ⅓N m⟨c²⟩.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Quote at least six postulates and identify which are idealisations — 'negligible molecular volume' and 'no intermolecular forces' generate all the limitations.  ·  Use R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ with SI units (kg, m³, Pa) in every speed calculation.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: r.m.s. speed c_rms = √(3RT/M); mean kinetic energy per mole = 3RT/2, per molecule = 3k_BT/2.  ·  Real gases deviate near condensation; Van der Waals: (P + a n²/V²)(V − nb) = nRT.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. Postulates (state them in order)  ·  • A gas consists of a very large number of extremely small molecules moving randomly and continuously in straight lines.  ·  • The actual volume of the molecules is negligible compared with the volume of the container — the gas is mostly empty space.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: PV = nRT  ·  c_rms = √(3RT/M)  ·  KE_mole = 3RT/2

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Collisions destroy kinetic energy. ✅ Collisions are elastic; energy is redistributed, not lost.  ·  ❌ Pressure is a continuous push by molecules. ✅ Pressure is the average rate of momentum transfer during wall collisions.  ·  ❌ The theory is equally valid at 200 atm. ✅ Ideal-gas assumptions break down at high pressure and low temperature.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ ideal gas equation pv = nrt; from kinetic theory p = ⅓ (nm/m)⟨c²⟩, so pv = ⅓n m⟨c²⟩..  ·  State the postulates of the kinetic theory and identify the idealisations among them.  ·  Derive PV = (1/3)mnc̄² and use it to obtain the ideal gas equation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Obtain expressions for rms, average and most probable speeds and arrange them in order.  ·  Calculate the rms speed of oxygen molecules at 300 K (M = 32 g mol⁻¹).  ·  Explain why hydrogen escapes the Earth's atmosphere more easily than oxygen.

rows.text: State the limitations of the kinetic theory of gases.  ·  one worked example for "Gaseous state: Kinetic theory of gas and its postulates" — check units / edge cases.  ·  recall card: definition → formula → limit → one error to avoid.
